Record Class TopicHeader

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
network.ike.docs.plugin.registry.TopicHeader
Record Components:
file - the file, relative to the scan root, with / separators
topic - whether the file declares a :topic-id: before its heading
id - the topic id, or null for a file that is not a topic
title - the first heading's text: the level-1 heading for a topic; for any other file the first heading of any level, so a chapter file that starts at == still has a title
level - the heading level of title() (1 for =), or 0 when the file has no heading
attributes - every :topic-*: attribute in declaration order, keyed without the topic- prefix
documentAttributes - every other :name: value attribute in the header, before the heading or in the contiguous block after it (doctype, toc, ...), in order
anchor - present, missing or mismatched for a topic; null for other files
charCount - characters from the anchor line (or the heading, when there is no anchor) to the end of the file
includes - the number of include:: lines in the file
findings - what is wrong with the header, empty when nothing is
public record TopicHeader(String file, boolean topic, String id, String title, int level, Map<String,String> attributes, Map<String,String> documentAttributes, String anchor, long charCount, int includes, List<String> findings) extends Record
The parsed header of one AsciiDoc file: the :topic-*: attribute block, the anchor and the level-1 heading, read line by line without AsciidoctorJ. The layout is the one IKE-ASCIIDOC-FRAGMENT.md prescribes: an optional comment header, the attribute block (values may continue on the next line with a trailing backslash), a literal [[anchor]] equal to the topic id, then = Title.

A file with no :topic-id: before its heading is not a topic; it is recorded as an assembly (when it carries include:: lines) or a plain file, with its title and document attributes, and gets no header findings. Every kind of module the doc pipeline renders is covered: topic libraries, assemblies, doc-only and hybrid projects.
